transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that I just feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore. It's like I just can't get comfortable, especially when I’m supposed to sit quietly and handle paperwork or, you know, go over shared household plans. Like the other day, my husband and I were trying to figure out the budget for this minor kitchen remodel we want to do. The contractor is actually a guy my sister recommended—she used him for her back patio and he did a really beautiful job, gorgeous stonework, but he is just terribly slow at returning emails. Anyway, we were sitting at the dining table with all these forms and quotes, and I just... I couldn't do it. I just can't sit quietly and focus on that kind of stuff without feeling like I need to jump out of my skin.

Can you describe what you mean by not being able to sit quietly or feeling like you need to jump out of your skin? Do you find yourself fidgeting, pacing, or feeling physically restless during these moments?

Yeah, exactly. It’s... well, like if we’re at a family dinner, or um, during church meetings, I’m usually twisting my wedding ring around and around, or bouncing my foot under the table. Actually, speaking of my ring, we had to take it in to get the band reinforced last year because I had worn it down so much just from messing with it all the time. We went to this little jeweler downtown, right next to that amazing bakery—oh, what’s it called? The one with the green awning that does those incredible lemon tarts. I used to try making lemon tarts from scratch when I first decided to stay home after college, but the pastry is just so finicky and makes a huge mess of the counters. 

But anyway, even when I’m trying really, really hard to look composed and polite at those meetings, I just can't stop shifting around in my chair. It drives my husband a little crazy. He always puts his hand on my knee under the table to stop it from bouncing, which is actually kind of nice because his hands are always so warm and I'm always freezing in that building, but... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, just... yeah, I'm always moving some part of my body.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or on edge even when you're not in those kinds of situations, like during the day when you're just at home or going about your regular routine?

Yeah, honestly, it's all day. Even when I have absolutely nowhere to be. Like, on days when I’m just at home, I’ll start doing the laundry—which, by the way, I recently switched to those eco-friendly detergent sheets because I read this huge article about plastic jugs in the ocean, and it’s just heartbreaking what’s happening to the sea turtles. My daughter actually did a project on sea turtles in fourth grade, she made this adorable little diorama out of a shoebox and some blue cellophane... wait, sorry. What was I talking about? 

Oh! Right, my routine at home. Yeah, so I'll go from the laundry, and then to checking my emails, and then suddenly I'm reorganizing a drawer in the kitchen, and then I'm checking the calendar... just bouncing around from thing to thing without really taking a break. It just feels like I’m being pushed from the inside, you know? Like I have to keep doing something and I can't just sit on the couch and just... exist.
Do you find that your mind often drifts or that you're easily distracted by things around you, even when you're trying to focus on a specific task?

Oh, absolutely. It's terrible. If I’m trying to, say, sit at the kitchen table and finally fill out those school forms for my kids—which they really need to digitize, by the way. I don't understand why in this day and age they still send home these huge stacks of paper. Last week, my son came home with a packet that was easily ten pages long, and it got completely soaked in his backpack because his water bottle leaked. We bought him one of those expensive stainless steel ones, thinking it would last forever, but the little silicone seal in the lid just popped right out. I meant to email the company about a replacement part, but... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, getting distracted. Yes. So, I'll be at the table trying to work on those forms, and my phone will buzz with a text, or I'll hear a car drive by outside, or I'll just suddenly think, "Oh, I need to take the chicken out of the freezer for dinner." And then I'm just completely off track. I'll be in the kitchen holding the chicken, or looking out the window, and I won't even realize I completely stopped what I was supposed to be doing until ten minutes later.
Do you ever feel overwhelmed by worry or fear, even when there's no immediate reason for concern?

Um, not really worry or fear, no. I mean, I definitely get stressed, but it's more about the chaos of everything I have to do, not like a deep dread or anything. Although, speaking of fear, my neighbor's dog—this huge, fluffy Bernese Mountain Dog named Barnaby—got loose the other day and came bounding into my yard while I was trying to plant some hydrangeas. They’re the limelight kind, the ones that start out kind of green and then turn white? My grandmother used to have a whole row of them along her driveway back in Ohio. We used to go visit her every summer, and she’d make these incredible peach cobblers with peaches right off the tree in her backyard. I tried planting a peach tree here a few years ago, but the soil just isn't right for it, I think. Or maybe I just forgot to water it enough when it was getting established. I'm terrible with watering schedules. 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Worrying? Yeah, no, I don't really have that overwhelmed, fearful feeling. It's just the restlessness and the distraction, mostly.
Do you often feel like you're talking more than usual, or find yourself interrupting others because you can't wait to get your thoughts out?

Yeah, I... I do do that. I really try not to, because I care a lot about being respectful, you know? It's important to me to be a good listener. But I still find myself jumping into my husband's conversations all the time. Like last night, he was on the phone with his brother, who just moved to Denver, actually. They bought this gorgeous mid-century modern house, but apparently the inspection missed a huge issue with the HVAC system, so they're freezing. Denver gets so cold. We went skiing there once before we had kids, and I completely wiped out on a green circle slope. I ended up with a bruised tailbone and had to sit on one of those donut pillows for a week. I couldn't even drive comfortably. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, interrupting. Right. So my husband will be talking, or anyone really, and I just... I finish their thoughts. It's like the response is already in my mouth and it just comes out before I've even made myself wait for them to finish. I don't mean to be rude, it just slips out so fast.
Do you often find yourself feeling irritable, short-tempered, or easily frustrated, especially when you're unable to stay focused or still?

No, I wouldn't say I get irritable or short-tempered. I mean, I get frustrated with myself when I can't get things done, but I don't really snap at people or get angry. My sister, on the other hand, she has a terrible temper. We were supposed to go to this pottery painting class together last weekend for her birthday. She loves that kind of stuff. She has this whole collection of hand-painted mugs that she's made over the years. They're actually really pretty, she does these intricate floral designs. She wanted to be an art major in college, but our parents really pushed her toward business, which is a shame because she's so talented. She ended up working in HR for a tech company, and she hates it. She says the corporate culture is just soul-crushing. They make them do all these team-building exercises that feel so forced, like virtual escape rooms and things like that. 

Anyway, where was I going with that? Oh, right, irritability. No, I don't really get short-tempered like she does. I'm usually pretty easygoing, just... scattered.
Have you noticed that you talk excessively during meetings or social interactions, even when you don't feel particularly excited or energized?

Um, I guess I do talk a lot, yeah. But I don't know if it's excessive? I mean, people tell me I'm chatty. Like at the PTA meetings—I volunteer for the PTA at my kids' school, mostly helping with the bake sales and the spring carnival. Last year we did a dunk tank for the carnival, and the principal actually volunteered to sit in it. It was so funny, the kids were lined up halfway across the field just for a chance to dunk him. My youngest son, Leo, he plays Little League, so he has a pretty good arm, and he managed to hit the target on his first try. The water was freezing, too, because they just filled it from the hose that morning. Speaking of hoses, I really need to buy a new one for the front yard. The one we have now has this kink in it that just won't come out, and it makes watering the hanging baskets on the porch such a hassle. I tried fixing it with duct tape, but that only lasted about two days before it started leaking again. Duct tape really isn't the miracle fix everyone says it is, you know? 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, talking a lot. Um, yeah, I'm not sure. I don't really pay attention to how much I'm talking compared to other people, to be honest. I just kind of talk.
Would you say that your level of talking or physical activity is noticeably more than what most adults around you typically display, even when the situation doesn’t call for it?

I think so, yeah. Physically, I just don't really stop. Like, on days when I’m home, I move from doing the laundry to checking my emails to reorganizing a drawer to checking the calendar, all without really taking a break. It feels like I’m being pushed from the inside, you know? Like there's this motor that just keeps me walking around the house. 

Speaking of the laundry, our dryer has been making this awful squeaking noise lately. It sounds exactly like a dying bird. My husband said he’d look at it, but he’s been so busy. He’s an accountant, and tax season is just brutal for him. He practically lives at the office from February to April. Last year, I tried to surprise him by bringing dinner to his office because he was working so late, but I had to slam on my brakes on the way there and I accidentally spilled the entire container of chicken parmesan all over the passenger seat of my car. Getting tomato sauce out of car upholstery is practically impossible, I swear. I tried club soda, baking soda, that special foam spray they sell at the auto parts store... the guy at the store was really nice, though. He had this adorable golden retriever behind the counter. I love goldens, we had one growing up named Buster, and he used to steal whole loaves of bread off the kitchen counter...

Wait, I'm sorry, I completely lost my train of thought. What was the question? Oh, right, moving more than other adults. Yeah, I definitely do. I see other moms just sitting on the couch watching a movie or reading, and I just can't do that. I always have to be up and doing something.
